newsitem.title: CANADA: ONTARIO HYDRO TO SHUT 7 NUCLEAR REACTORS - REPORTS.
newsitem.headline: ONTARIO HYDRO TO SHUT 7 NUCLEAR REACTORS - REPORTS.

text.p: Provincially owned Ontario Hydro is expected to announce at a news conference at 1100 EDT/1500 GMT on Wednesday that it will temporarily shut down seven of its nuclear reactors at a cost of C$5 billion to C$8 billion, media reports said.
Ontario Hydro, North America's largest power utility, was shutting the reactors for a major overhaul, the reports said.
They quoted Ontario Hydro Chairman William Farlinger as saying the overhaul would not increase the price of electricity in Canada's most populous province.
Late on Tuesday, the utility said that Chief Executive Allan Kupcis resigned after an unfavorable internal report on the nuclear division, which he had commissioned.

To make up for the loss in production from nuclear plants, Ontario Hydro will increase electricity production from its fossil-fuel plants at Nanticoke and Lambton, Ontario. Ontario Hydro would also put into production mothballed units at the Lennox plant near Napanee, Ontario reports said.
The reports said the utility estimated that the moves would cost between C$5 billion and C$8 billion from 1997 to 2001.
The increased costs include upgrades to the nuclear plants, the replacement of uranium with more expensive fossil fuel and other capital and operating costs, reports said.
Ontario Hydro was also considering writing off $2 billion in unproductive assets in the current fiscal year, the reports said.
Over the next three years, Ontario Hydro would overhaul the Bruce B, Pickering B and Darlington nuclear power plants, the reports said.
